# Template for grammars/pma.parg, the grammar of pma (dialect P, "plurimath
# ascii"). Do not edit the generated .parg by hand: edit this file or
# data/vocabulary.json and run
#   ruby scripts/generate_grammar.rb
# Placeholders (a name in double braces) are replaced by generated text.
# Lines that start with `#!` are template-only notes and are not copied.
#
# GENERATED by scripts/generate_grammar.rb -- do not edit.
# pma (dialect P) grammar, plurimath docs/pma.adoc (amath#16).
# registry data/vocabulary.json amath-vocabulary/v2 edition 1 sha256:768016984baee3ea142b69f0f31f4b9e9255ddedea078d6c7fb1728dc718695c
# unit(...) content: asciiunits 0.1.6 artifact sha256:aa22618c80dc02f3fe1edf2c798dbe34aceae5f4d84524ff98f76a2b91af151d
# reserved words (terminals): unit ustd uexp ucov diff quantity
#
# Version 1 reads one term: a measured value (a measured literal or one of
# the constructors ustd, uexp, ucov), optionally with a trailing unit(...),
# a unit(...) on its own, or diff(...) of a measured value with its unit.
# Whitespace may stand between tokens and never inside one. `ustd(`,
# `uexp(`, `ucov(`, `unit(` and `diff(` are single tokens, so a reserved
# word followed by whitespace matches nothing. The content of unit(...) is
# captured as text and parsed by the asciiunits artifact (see
# Amath::Pma); its brackets nest at most 8 deep. A unit may be
# followed by `::` and one quantity name (the quantity assertion).

grammar Pma version "1.0.0" {
  any_char = %x00-10FFFF
  ws = " " / "\t" / "\n" / "\r" / %x0B / %x0C
  sp = *(ws)
  digit = %x30-39
  pma_number = 1*(digit) ["." 1*(digit)]
  pma_value = ["-"] pma_number

  # Distribution tags: the registry's pma distribution names, longest first.
  distribution_name = "arcsine" / "triang" / "rect"
  distribution_tag = "~" (distribution_name) as distribution
  shared_exponent = "e" (["+" / "-"] 1*(digit)) as shared_exponent
  interval_kind = "shortest" / "symmetric"

  # Measured literals: (v +/- u), (v +/- p%), with an optional tag inside
  # the bracket after the uncertainty; only the absolute form takes a
  # shared exponent.
  ml_relative = "(" sp (pma_value) as value sp ("+/-") as plus_minus sp (pma_number) as relative_magnitude "%" [sp distribution_tag] sp ")"
  ml_absolute = "(" sp (pma_value) as value sp ("+/-") as plus_minus sp (pma_number) as magnitude [sp distribution_tag] sp ")" [shared_exponent]
  measured_literal = ml_relative / ml_absolute

  # Constructors.
  ctor_sep = sp "," sp
  ustd_ctor = ("ustd") as uncertainty_class "(" sp (pma_value) as value ctor_sep (pma_number) as magnitude sp ")"
  uexp_ctor = ("uexp") as uncertainty_class "(" sp (pma_value) as value ctor_sep (pma_number) as magnitude ctor_sep (pma_number) as coverage_factor [ctor_sep (pma_number) as coverage_probability] sp ")"
  ucov_ctor = ("ucov") as uncertainty_class "(" sp (pma_value) as value ctor_sep (pma_number) as lower ctor_sep (pma_number) as upper ctor_sep (pma_number) as coverage_probability [ctor_sep (interval_kind) as interval_kind] sp ")"
  measured = measured_literal / ustd_ctor / uexp_ctor / ucov_ctor

  # unit(...): the unit expression text, brackets balanced to a fixed depth.
  # A run of whitespace inside it is kept only before more content.
  unit_char = !("(" / ")" / ws / "::") any_char
  unit_chunk_0 = unit_char / "(" sp *(unit_chunk_1) sp ")" / 1*(ws) &(unit_char / "(")
  unit_chunk_1 = unit_char / "(" sp *(unit_chunk_2) sp ")" / 1*(ws) &(unit_char / "(")
  unit_chunk_2 = unit_char / "(" sp *(unit_chunk_3) sp ")" / 1*(ws) &(unit_char / "(")
  unit_chunk_3 = unit_char / "(" sp *(unit_chunk_4) sp ")" / 1*(ws) &(unit_char / "(")
  unit_chunk_4 = unit_char / "(" sp *(unit_chunk_5) sp ")" / 1*(ws) &(unit_char / "(")
  unit_chunk_5 = unit_char / "(" sp *(unit_chunk_6) sp ")" / 1*(ws) &(unit_char / "(")
  unit_chunk_6 = unit_char / "(" sp *(unit_chunk_7) sp ")" / 1*(ws) &(unit_char / "(")
  unit_chunk_7 = unit_char / "(" sp *(unit_chunk_8) sp ")" / 1*(ws) &(unit_char / "(")
  unit_chunk_8 = unit_char / 1*(ws) &(unit_char)

  # The quantity assertion: `::` and a quantity name after the unit
  # expression, at most one. The name is text up to the closing bracket;
  # its own brackets balance one deep (unitsdb names such as
  # "ratio logarithm (Np)"). Whether the name is a unitsdb quantity is
  # checked by Amath::Pma, not here.
  quantity_chunk_0 = unit_char / "(" *(quantity_chunk_1) ")" / 1*(ws) &(unit_char / "(")
  quantity_chunk_1 = unit_char / 1*(ws) &(unit_char)
  quantity_ref = 1*(quantity_chunk_0)
  unit_plain = (1*(unit_chunk_0)) as literal / "" as empty_list
  unit_asserted = (1*(unit_chunk_0)) as literal sp "::" sp (quantity_ref) as quantity
  unit_ctor = "unit(" sp (unit_asserted / unit_plain) as unit sp ")"

  # A measured value carries its unit inside the uncertainty node, as the
  # dialect L "unitsml(...)" argument does.
  attached = (measured sp unit_ctor) as uncertainty
  bare = (measured) as uncertainty
  diff_ctor = "diff(" sp (attached) as diff sp ")"
  term = diff_ctor / attached / bare / unit_ctor
  document = sp (term) as term sp
}

entry document: document

bindings document { term -> term (any) }
